title: salix cordata subsp. rigida
intro: Salix cordata subsp. rigida, commonly known as the stiff-leaved willow, is a type of deciduous shrub or small tree that belongs to the Salicaceae family. The plant is known for its slender branches and narrow, pointed leaves that are a dark green color on top and a lighter green on the underside. Salix cordata subsp. rigida has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and is said to help with pain relief and wound healing. The plant's therapeutic actions are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including salicin, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which have been shown to have analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects.
